      Masses and Springs

             Khalil Iskarous
     Department of Linguistics

Principles of Mass-Spring Systems




   1.  Mass ↑ Frequency ↓, Stiffness ↑ Frequency ↑
   2.  An n-mass system has n modes of vibration, each with a higher frequency
   3.  An m’s increase lowers frequency proportionally to how much the mass moves,
      which depends on where it is!
   4.  A k’s increase raises frequency proportionally to how much the spring
       stretches/compresses, which depends on where it is!
   5.  Where there’s maximal movement, there’s no stretching, An where there’s maximal
        stretching, there’s no movement!
   6.   In a Fixed-Fixed System, the harmonics are multiples of the base frequency, because
       the base mode fits n-times into each successive mode
   7.   In a Fixed-Free System, the formants are odd multiples of the base frequency,
      because the base mode fits an odd n-times into each successive mode

When we compress air, as happens in a constriction, its stiffness
rises, so making a constriction at a place that experiences lots of
compression, will raise frequency. And bunching up air makes its
mas//density larger, so in a part of the vocal tract where air moves a
lot, constricting raises mass! So making a constriction increases
mass and increases stiffness.

But be careful!!!! This doesn’t mean that constrictions have no effect
on frequency!!! Why? Because the parts of a vibrating medium that
moves the most alternate with those that compress/uncompress
the most!
